notes.title: Version 3.0 released
notes.content:
With version 3.0, the map is placed right in the center of the gameplay experience. The result? Smoother navigation and better overview, making it easier to focus on the story and making critical decisions.

Some other user interface changes have been made as well, like scrapping the panning when switching between views.

The option to fast travel has been extended to a few more places, and some typos have been fixed.

notes.title: Version 2.0 released
notes.content:
Bloodwood Dungeon is heavily inspired by classical, old-school gamebooks from the eighties and nineties, with their simple battle systems based on dice rolls. With this update, the game goes all the way and makes the mechanics of combat explicit with dice rolls on screen, showing more clearly where randomly generated numbers play a part in the flow of battle.

Some other graphical flourishes are introduced as well, like red bars showing the remaining hit points for player and opponent alike.

The option to fast travel has been extended to a few more places, and some minor issues with descriptions have been fixed.

notes.title: Version 1.3 released
notes.content:
In version 1.3 of Bloodwood Dungeon:

* A new colorful character is introduced that may aid the player in ways not to be disclosed here.

* Two new achievements.

* Some typos removed.

notes.title: Version 1.2
notes.content: Some enemy encounters have been improved by increasing player agency.

notes.title: Version 1.1
notes.content:
Players have pointed out specific areas for improvement. This update addresses some of these, namely:

* There is now an additional save spot earlier in the game, just after chapter 1.
* A few characters have been added in the forest area.
* Some minor bugs have been removed.

notes.title: Patch 1.01
notes.content:
* Some fight balancing issues addressed
* Introduced additional character
* Typos corrected
